differentials: Spinal cord compression due to metastatic tumor

shortlist: Spinal cord compression due to metastatic tumor

shortlist.label: Traumatic spinal cord injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with quadriplegia and spinal cord compression after a fall

shortlist.label: Cervical spine fracture
shortlist.why_kept: MRI showed anterolisthesis at C4 and C5, consistent with a fracture

shortlist.label: Spinal cord compression due to metastatic tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, spinal cord compression can be caused by a tumor

shortlist.label: Acute transverse myelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with complete sensory loss and reduced diffusion in spinal cord white matter

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with hypothermia and autonomic dysfunction, which can be seen in spinal epidural abscess

raw.rationale: The patient's history of falling out of bed and the MRI findings of spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis are consistent with a traumatic injury to the spinal cord.

rejected.label: Cervical spine fracture
rejected.why: While possible, the primary issue appears to be spinal cord injury rather than just a fracture.

rejected.label: Spinal cord compression due to metastatic tumor
rejected.why: There is no mention of a tumor, and the acute presentation after a fall suggests trauma rather than a tumor.

rejected.label: Acute transverse myelitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are more consistent with a traumatic injury than an inflammatory process like myelitis.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: There is no mention of infection or abscess on imaging, making this diagnosis less likely.
